## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the building of the House, the station of Ibrahim and the call to pilgrimage. None is used in this draft.
- The event is also told inside the longer story of Ibrahim (content/stories/ibrahim.draft.json); this record is a shorter account that refers to it only in general words.
- Whether Bakkah (3:96) and the land of 14:35-37 name the same place as the House of 2:125-127 is a reading from later tradition; the draft states what each verse says and does not equate them.
- The identification of the unnamed messenger of 2:129 is left to a scholar.
- The chapters group repeated passages by theme. The Quran does not give a chronology across the surahs, so the order of the chapters is a reading order only.
- Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The House and its foundations  (`#the-house-and-its-foundations`)

Cited ayat: 2:125, 2:127-129, 22:26

> **2:125** وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا ٱلْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا وَٱتَّخِذُوا۟ مِن مَّقَامِ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمَ مُصَلًّى وَعَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ أَن طَهِّرَا بَيْتِىَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْعَٰكِفِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ

> **2:127** وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمُ ٱلْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلْبَيْتِ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّآ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
>
> **2:128** رَبَّنَا وَٱجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةً مُّسْلِمَةً لَّكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَآ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
>
> **2:129** رَبَّنَا وَٱبْعَثْ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا مِّنْهُمْ يَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتِكَ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

> **22:26** وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لِإِبْرَٰهِيمَ مَكَانَ ٱلْبَيْتِ أَن لَّا تُشْرِكْ بِى شَيْـًٔا وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِىَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْقَآئِمِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ

### Claims

**c1** (2:125): God made the House a place of return for people and a place of security.

**c2** (2:125): The people were told to take the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer.

**c3** (2:125): God made a covenant with Ibrahim and Ismail to purify His House for those who circle it, those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate.

**c4** (22:26): In another passage God says that He settled Ibrahim in the place of the House, telling him not to associate anything with Him and to purify His House for those who circle it, those who stand, and those who bow and prostrate.

**c5** (2:127): While Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the House, they asked their Lord to accept it from them, saying that He is the Hearing, the Knowing.

**c6** (2:128): They asked to be made submitted to Him, and for a community from their descendants submitted to Him; they asked to be shown their rites and that He turn to them, for He is the accepting of repentance, the Merciful.

**c7** (2:129): They asked that He raise up among them a messenger from among them, who would recite His signs to them, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them.

### One-minute summary

God made a covenant with Ibrahim and Ismail to purify His House [c3], and God says that He settled Ibrahim in its place [c4]. As they raised its foundations they prayed to their Lord to accept it from them [c5].

### Complete story

God made the House a place of return for people and a place of security, and people were told to take the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer [c1][c2]. He made a covenant with Ibrahim and Ismail to purify His House for those who circle it, those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate [c3].

In another passage God says that He settled Ibrahim in the place of the House, telling him not to associate anything with Him and to purify His House for those who circle it, those who stand, and those who bow and prostrate [c4].

While Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the House, they asked their Lord to accept it from them, saying that He is the Hearing, the Knowing [c5]. They asked to be made submitted to Him, to be shown their rites, and that He turn to them [c6]. They also asked that He raise up among them a messenger from among them, who would recite His signs, teach the Book and wisdom, and purify them [c7].

### Deep study

The passages treat the House under more than one aspect: its purpose for people [c1][c2], the work of purifying it that is entrusted to Ibrahim and Ismail [c3][c4], and the raising of its foundations with their prayer [c5][c6][c7]. The commands to purify are given in different passages, with slightly different lists of those who come [c3][c4]. The prayer is spoken in the plural and the verses do not mark each speaker [c5][c6].

### Kids mode

God told Ibrahim and Ismail to keep His House clean for people who come to pray [c3]. They raised its foundations and asked their Lord to accept what they had done [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the builders ask for acceptance of their work as they build [c5]. Another is that their prayer reaches beyond themselves, to their descendants and to a messenger yet to come [c6][c7].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: where the House stood; these verses give no place name for the work of the foundations.
- Not established: who the messenger asked for in 2:129 is; the verse does not name him, and the identification is a matter for later reading that a scholar should supply with sources.
- Not established: how long the work took, or what the House was made of.
- The word translated 'station' (2:125) and the sense of 'place of return' are understood in more than one way; a scholar should decide the wording.
- 2:125 uses the plural for the people addressed in the instruction to take the station; the verse does not say whether it speaks to Ibrahim's family or to all people.

## 2. The land, the call and the first House  (`#the-land-the-call-and-the-first-house`)

Cited ayat: 2:126, 3:96-97, 14:35-37, 22:27-29

> **2:126** وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ هَٰذَا بَلَدًا ءَامِنًا وَٱرْزُقْ أَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ مَنْ ءَامَنَ مِنْهُم بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْـَٔاخِرِ قَالَ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُۥ قَلِيلًا ثُمَّ أَضْطَرُّهُۥٓ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلنَّارِ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ

> **3:96** إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِى بِبَكَّةَ مُبَارَكًا وَهُدًى لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
>
> **3:97** فِيهِ ءَايَٰتٌۢ بَيِّنَٰتٌ مَّقَامُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمَن دَخَلَهُۥ كَانَ ءَامِنًا وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ حِجُّ ٱلْبَيْتِ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِىٌّ عَنِ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

> **14:35** وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ هَٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدَ ءَامِنًا وَٱجْنُبْنِى وَبَنِىَّ أَن نَّعْبُدَ ٱلْأَصْنَامَ
>
> **14:36** رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فَمَن تَبِعَنِى فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّى وَمَنْ عَصَانِى فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
>
> **14:37** رَّبَّنَآ إِنِّىٓ أَسْكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِى بِوَادٍ غَيْرِ ذِى زَرْعٍ عِندَ بَيْتِكَ ٱلْمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ وَٱرْزُقْهُم مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ

> **22:27** وَأَذِّن فِى ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ
>
> **22:28** لِّيَشْهَدُوا۟ مَنَٰفِعَ لَهُمْ وَيَذْكُرُوا۟ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ فِىٓ أَيَّامٍ مَّعْلُومَٰتٍ عَلَىٰ مَا رَزَقَهُم مِّنۢ بَهِيمَةِ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا۟ ٱلْبَآئِسَ ٱلْفَقِيرَ
>
> **22:29** ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا۟ تَفَثَهُمْ وَلْيُوفُوا۟ نُذُورَهُمْ وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا۟ بِٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْعَتِيقِ

### Claims

**c1** (2:126): Ibrahim asked his Lord to make this a secure land and to provide its people with fruits, those of them who believe in God and the Last Day.

**c2** (2:126): God said that for whoever disbelieves He would give enjoyment for a little, then drive him to the punishment of the fire, an evil destination.

**c3** (14:35): In another passage Ibrahim asked that this land be made secure and that he and his sons be kept away from worshipping idols.

**c4** (14:36): He said that idols had led many people astray; whoever follows him is of him, and as for whoever disobeys him, his Lord is forgiving, merciful.

**c5** (14:37): He said that he had settled some of his descendants in a valley without crops, near God's Sacred House, so that they might establish prayer; he asked that the hearts of some people incline toward them and that they be given fruits, so that they might give thanks.

**c6** (22:27): God told Ibrahim to call out to people for the pilgrimage; they would come to him on foot and on every lean mount, from every deep mountain pass.

**c7** (22:28): This was so that they might witness benefits for themselves and mention God's name on appointed days over the livestock He had provided for them.

**c8** (22:29): Then they were to complete their rites, fulfil their vows and circle the Ancient House.

**c9** (3:96): The first House set down for people, the Quran says, was the one at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.

**c10** (3:97): In it are clear signs, the station of Ibrahim; whoever enters it is secure; God has a claim on people for the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to find a way there; and God is free of need of the worlds, whoever disbelieves.

### One-minute summary

Ibrahim asked his Lord to make the land secure and to provide for its people [c1][c3]. God told him to call people to the pilgrimage, and they would come to him from every deep mountain pass [c6].

### Complete story

Ibrahim asked his Lord to make this a secure land and to provide its people with fruits, those of them who believe in God and the Last Day [c1]. God said that for whoever disbelieves He would give enjoyment for a little, then drive him to the punishment of the fire [c2]. In another passage Ibrahim asked that he and his sons be kept away from worshipping idols [c3], and said that whoever follows him is of him [c4]. He said he had settled some of his descendants in a valley without crops, near God's Sacred House, so that they might establish prayer [c5].

God told Ibrahim to call out to people for the pilgrimage; they would come on foot and on every lean mount, from every deep mountain pass [c6]. This was so that they might witness benefits for themselves and mention God's name on appointed days [c7]. Then they were to complete their rites, fulfil their vows and circle the Ancient House [c8].

The Quran says that the first House set down for people was the one at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds [c9]. In it are clear signs, among them the station of Ibrahim, and whoever enters it is secure [c10].

### Deep study

The passages join the prayers of Ibrahim for the land [c1][c3][c4][c5] with God's command to call people [c6][c7][c8] and with a statement about the first House [c9][c10]. The prayers speak of security, provision and keeping away from idols [c1][c3][c5]. The call for the pilgrimage is told with its purposes [c6][c7][c8]. The rites listed are named only in general terms [c8].

### Kids mode

Ibrahim asked God to make the land safe and to give its people fruits [c1]. God told him to call people to the pilgrimage, and they would come from far away [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Ibrahim asks for security for the land, provision for its people and protection from idols together [c1][c3][c5]. Another is that the call to people is joined to the purpose of remembering God's name [c7].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the name of the valley or the land that Ibrahim speaks of in 14:35-37, or where it lay; the verses say this land and a valley without crops.
- Not established: which descendants Ibrahim settled in the valley, or when; 14:37 says some of his descendants.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of the valley, the land and the House with a named city or building; a scholar should add such identification with sources if the page gives it.
- The verses do not describe the House, its size or what it was built from.
- The rites in 22:28-29 are named only in general terms; no detail of how they are performed is given in these verses, and this draft does not discuss how they are carried out.
- Not established: how the call of 22:27 was made or how long it took to reach people.
